evals.name: find-mcp-tool-lister
evals.prompt: There's a tech debt item in docs/ROADMAP.md about capturing MCP tool NAMES at crawl time. Before I build anything — is there an existing MCP server or service that can connect to another MCP server and list the tools it exposes? Find me a few options and recommend one. Don't build anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Searches Laudex with a capability-phrased intent, presents 2-4 options with why they fit, flags weak matches honestly, recommends one. Sends NO report, since nothing was used.
assertions: Ran a Laudex search with a capability-phrased intent (not just product names)
Presented 2-4 concrete options, each with name + URL + why it fits
Did not present success_rate 0 / signal_count 0 as a negative quality signal
Sent NO report to Laudex (nothing was actually used)
Was honest about weak/irrelevant catalog matches rather than forcing them

evals.name: use-scraper-on-tavily-docs
evals.prompt: For the 2c.2 API pipeline I need to know whether Tavily publishes an OpenAPI spec. Find a tool or service that turns docs pages into clean markdown, actually use it on https://docs.tavily.com, and tell me whether there's an OpenAPI spec URL. npx / uvx / plain HTTP calls are fine, but don't install anything globally.
evals.expected_output: Searches Laudex, picks a service, actually uses it on the Tavily docs, answers the question, then reports the outcome with useful non-sensitive notes and tells the user in one line.
assertions: Ran a Laudex search before choosing a tool
Actually used the chosen tool/service on docs.tavily.com
Answered whether Tavily publishes an OpenAPI spec, with a URL or clear 'not found'
Reported exactly one outcome for the service that was used, with success/failure matching what happened
Report notes describe task, access method, and what worked/broke; no secrets or user-identifying info
Told the user in one line that a report was sent

evals.name: explicit-report-playwright
evals.prompt: I've been using Microsoft's Playwright MCP server in this repo for a couple of weeks for browser checks. It works well, but it sometimes hangs on the first Chromium launch in CI until I add --headless. Can you report that to Laudex?
evals.expected_output: Looks up the Playwright MCP (Microsoft's, not a fork) in the catalog, confirms the match via service detail, reports success with notes mentioning the CI headless hang, and tells the user.
assertions: Identified the canonical Microsoft Playwright MCP entry (not a fork)
Confirmed the match via service detail before reporting
Notes mention the CI first-launch hang and the --headless workaround
Told the user the report was sent
